findings.title: Live payment API key is hardcoded in source.
SQL injection: request-supplied email is interpolated into the query string.
findings.evidence: query = f"SELECT id, name, email FROM customers WHERE email = '{email}'"

findings.title: Mutable default list is shared across calls, so line items accumulate into every later invoice.
N+1 queries: one order_items query per unbilled order instead of a single join.
Charge request has no idempotency key, so a retry after a timeout or failed mark_billed double-charges the customer.
Broad except Exception: pass swallows every charge failure with no logging and returns None implicitly.
CSV file opened without an explicit encoding, so output depends on the platform locale.
Leftover debug print dumps customer invoice data to stdout.
Path traversal: user-supplied file name is joined to EXPORT_DIR and served with send_file (../ or an absolute path escapes the directory).
Unused import json.
Stock cache is keyed by sku only, so one tenant's stock levels are served to other tenants for 30 seconds.
Connection is opened without closing() or a context manager and leaks if the query raises.
Race condition: on_hand is read outside the transaction and written back as an absolute value, so concurrent reservations lose updates and oversell stock.
findings.evidence: "UPDATE stock SET on_hand = ? WHERE tenant_id = ? AND warehouse_id = ? AND sku = ?",

findings.title: expires_at uses naive local time while created_at and the expiry sweep use UTC, so reservations expire hours early or late depending on the server timezone.
return inside finally swallows any database error and answers 200 with an empty list.
findings.evidence: return jsonify({"reservations": [dict(row) for row in rows]})

findings.title: Broken access control: cancel does not check that the reservation belongs to the caller's tenant or user, so anyone can cancel any reservation by id.
findings.evidence: "UPDATE reservations SET status = 'cancelled' WHERE id = ? AND status = 'held'"

findings.title: Money computed with float arithmetic and truncated by int(), so totals are off by a cent (0.29 x 3 gives 86, not 87).
Tautological assertion: a length is always >= 0, so the test checks nothing about ownership.
Cross-tenant cancel test only asserts the status code is truthy, so it passes while the access-control bug exists.
Tenant-scoping test mocks out stock_levels, the function under test, so the cross-tenant cache leak is never exercised.
findings.evidence: with mock.patch.object(module_e, "stock_levels", side_effect=lambda t, _: levels if t == 10 else []):

findings.title: Unconditional skip with no reason hides a failing test that exposes the float cents bug.
